items.title: Intravenous iron supplementation in heart failure and iron deficiency: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

ai.headline: Intravenous iron may reduce heart failure hospitalisation, but evidence on mortality and function remains uncertain.
ai.summary: This umbrella review examined 18 systematic reviews of intravenous iron in people with heart failure and iron deficiency. It found the most consistent link was with fewer heart failure hospitalisations, while effects on death, fitness and quality of life were uncertain due to low-quality reviews and overlapping trials.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a common treatment for iron deficiency in heart failure may help keep people out of hospital, but the evidence is not yet strong enough to be certain.
ai.life_skill: If you have heart failure, discuss iron status and treatment options with your cardiologist or GP rather than assuming supplements will help.
ai.fact: Iron deficiency is common in heart failure and is linked to exercise intolerance, poorer health and repeated hospitalisation.

quiz.question: What outcome did the reviews most consistently link to intravenous iron in heart failure?
quiz.answer: Reduced heart failure hospitalisation, including recurrent hospitalisation and combined hospitalisation-cardiovascular death endpoints.

ai.caveat: The underlying reviews had low methodological quality, trials were substantially overlapping, and certainty of evidence was low or very low for most outcomes.

items.title: Psychological preparation in multimodal cancer prehabilitation: a systematic review and meta-synthesis of patients’ experiences

ai.headline: Psychological preparation in cancer prehabilitation comes from the whole programme, not just psychological support.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-synthesis looked at 17 qualitative studies involving 230 adults who took part in multimodal cancer prehabilitation combining exercise, nutrition and psychological support. Patients experienced psychological preparation as having something to act on, discovering what their bodies could do, understanding what was coming, being taken seriously, and not being alone. These benefits arose through exercise, dietary support and relationships with staff and peers, not only explicitly psychological input.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how cancer prehabilitation is delivered and matched to patients can shape their ability to cope before treatment.
ai.life_skill: Notice which parts of a support programme feel most useful to you and tell your care team so they can match help to what you can use.
ai.fact: Psychological preparation in cancer prehabilitation can arise from exercise, dietary support and relationships with staff and peers, not only explicitly psychological input.

quiz.question: According to the review, where did patients say psychological preparation came from?
quiz.answer: It arose through exercise, dietary support and relationships with staff and peers, not only explicitly psychological input.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and evidence came almost entirely from people who engaged with prehabilitation, with staff training, adherence and fidelity sparsely reported.

items.title: Adolescents' mental health, well-being, and biopsychological stress in school: a narrative review of school-related correlates and interventions

ai.headline: Schools can support adolescent mental health through relationships, skills, and targeted interventions, though results vary.
ai.summary: This narrative review examined research on adolescents' mental health, well-being, and stress in school settings. It found that supportive teacher and peer relationships, along with individual skills like coping and motivation, are linked to positive development, while school-based interventions such as social and emotional learning and mindfulness show mixed effectiveness.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that academic progress and student well-being can support each other rather than compete.
ai.life_skill: Notice which school relationships and habits help you feel calmer and more capable.
ai.fact: Mental health is more than the absence of mental illness; it includes positive well-being and functioning.

quiz.question: What does the review say about the effectiveness of school-based mental health interventions?
quiz.answer: Findings remain heterogeneous, particularly regarding intervention effectiveness.

ai.caveat: A narrative review summarises existing studies rather than providing new, pooled evidence, and the authors note that findings are mixed and more rigorous research is needed.

items.title: Depression in Women on a Global Level: Cultural Perspectives, Social Determinants, Gender Inequalities, and Implications for Mental Health Care
items.venue: British journal of healthcare and medical research

ai.headline: Women worldwide have higher rates of depression than men, shaped by social and cultural factors.
ai.summary: This review examined research on depression among women globally. It found women consistently experience higher rates than men, linked to poverty, violence, caregiving, reproductive health, and barriers to care, with cultural beliefs affecting how symptoms are expressed and treated.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how social conditions and culture influence mental health, helping people recognise that depression is not just an individual problem.
ai.life_skill: Notice how stress, relationships, and life changes affect your mood, and consider speaking to a trusted person or professional if low mood persists.
ai.fact: Depression is a leading cause of disability worldwide.

quiz.question: Do women consistently experience higher rates of depression than men across diverse contexts?
quiz.answer: Yes, the review found women consistently experience higher rates of depression than men across diverse cultural, social, and economic contexts.

ai.caveat: This is an integrative review synthesising existing literature rather than new primary evidence, so findings depend on the quality of the studies included.

items.title: Community burden of diphtheria during the 2023-24 epidemic in Kano State, Nigeria: a population-based household survey

ai.headline: A household survey found diphtheria was more common in Kano communities than official clinic records showed.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed nearly 8,000 people in four Nigerian local government areas during the 2023-24 diphtheria epidemic. They estimated a community attack rate of 1.1%, about three times the rate notified at three treatment sites, and found most deaths happened at home.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that clinic records can miss a large share of illness in the community, so outbreaks may be bigger than official figures suggest.
ai.life_skill: Check that your routine vaccinations are up to date and seek care quickly if you develop a serious sore throat or breathing difficulty.
ai.fact: Diphtheria is a serious infectious disease that can cause severe throat swelling and breathing problems.

quiz.question: How did the community attack rate compare with the rate notified at treatment sites?
quiz.answer: The community attack rate was about three times higher than the rate notified at three treatment sites.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and diphtheria, deaths and vaccination status were reported by respondents without laboratory or record confirmation.

items.title: College Success: Understanding the Roles of Financial Aid, Loans, Preparation, and Incentives -- by Douglas N. Harris, Christopher R. Taber, Alan Yang

ai.headline: Better college preparation may raise attainment more than financial aid alone.
ai.summary: The study models how financial aid, loans, incentives and pre-college skills affect college attendance and graduation. It finds most financial policies have moderate effects on attendance but small effects on completion, while better preparing students for college offers the greatest potential to increase attainment.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that money alone may not be enough to help more students finish college, and that skills before starting matter greatly.
ai.life_skill: Focus on building study and academic skills before starting college rather than relying only on financial support.
ai.fact: The earnings gap between college graduates and non-graduates has widened substantially over the past four decades.

quiz.question: What does the study find has the greatest potential for increasing college attainment?
quiz.answer: Better preparing students for college.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint using a simulation model rather than direct experimental proof, so the findings are not yet peer-reviewed or definitive.

items.title: Delayed Retirement, Intergenerational Transfers, and Fertility

ai.headline: Delaying retirement may cut grandparental childcare and lower fertility, especially for lower-income women.
ai.summary: The study models China’s gradual delayed-retirement reform and its effects on older adults’ work, money transfers to adult children, and grandparental childcare. Simulations suggest that while delayed retirement raises older employment and monetary transfers, it reduces childcare enough to lower fertility and older adults’ welfare, with larger losses among lower-income women. Childcare subsidies could offset these declines.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that retirement policy can affect family life and fertility through grandparental childcare, not just older adults’ work and income.
ai.life_skill: Notice how changes in grandparents’ work might affect the childcare they can provide to families.
ai.fact: Delayed retirement can reduce grandparental childcare even as it increases monetary transfers to adult children.

quiz.question: What happens to fertility when delayed retirement reduces grandparental childcare more than it increases monetary transfers?
quiz.answer: Fertility declines.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and relies on a model and simulations rather than direct observation of the reform’s outcomes.

items.title: Rethinking Consciousness: The Self-Organising Information-Processing Systems Hypothesis

ai.headline: A new theory suggests consciousness emerges from how information is organised and shared within systems, not just from biology.
ai.summary: The paper proposes the Self-Organising Information-Processing Systems Hypothesis. It suggests that when components interact and share information flexibly, they can develop capabilities like perception, memory and agency, and that consciousness may arise when awareness-related information supports flexible cognition.
ai.why_it_matters: It offers a way to think about consciousness that could apply to brains, artificial intelligence and group behaviour rather than treating it as unique to humans.
ai.life_skill: Notice how different groups or systems you are part of share information to make decisions together.
ai.fact: Consciousness is proposed as a configuration in which awareness-related information participates in flexible cognition.

quiz.question: According to the SOIPS hypothesis, is consciousness limited to human biology?
quiz.answer: No, consciousness is not restricted by definition to human biology.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint and a theoretical proposal, not peer-reviewed evidence or experimental proof.

items.title: Pedagogical resilience reconstruction in the AI era: a longitudinal reflexive thematic analysis of teacher reflective journals

ai.headline: Keeping an AI course running does not automatically mean students are learning.
ai.summary: The study followed one teacher's reflective journals over a 12-week AI course for first-year art students. The teacher found that students often mistook seeing, bookmarking, or one-click generation for actual ability, especially when teaching became demonstration-only and the final assessment did not require attendance.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that high engagement with AI tools can hide a lack of real learning, which matters for anyone studying independently.
ai.life_skill: Check whether you can actually do the task yourself without watching a demo or using a one-click tool.
ai.fact: Students can appear highly engaged with AI tools while gaining little actual learning.

quiz.question: What did the teacher call the pattern where students treated seeing or one-click generation as being able to do?
quiz.answer: The teacher termed it a teacher-perceived low-threshold illusion.

ai.caveat: This is a single teacher's self-study based on their own journals, so the findings are not proof and cannot be generalised to all students or courses.

items.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders

ai.headline: A new method helps AI link map locations with satellite images and other data more effectively.
ai.summary: The study examined location encoders, which turn geographic coordinates into digital descriptions using satellite imagery. It found these tools are mathematically limited to two dimensions, but a new two-stage method called LoCA overcomes this by creating a shared, high-quality target from satellite data and training location and metadata encoders to match it.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because better location encoding can improve how we monitor land cover, wildfires, biodiversity and climate from space.
ai.life_skill: Try checking how satellite maps are used to track environmental changes in your area.
ai.fact: Location encoders convert geographic coordinates into high-dimensional digital descriptors using Earth observation imagery.

quiz.question: What did the researchers prove about standard location encoders?
quiz.answer: They proved that any Lipschitz location encoder produces an output of intrinsic dimension at most 2.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet established.

items.title: Comparing Embedded and End-of-Session Formative Quizzes: Implications for Engagement and Self-Regulated Learning in Psychology Classrooms

ai.headline: Short quizzes spread through a lecture boosted engagement and self-regulated learning more than quizzes at the end.
ai.summary: Researchers compared embedded quizzes during psychology lectures with the same quizzes given at the end of lectures among 81 third-year students. Students who took quizzes during the lecture reported higher cognitive engagement, situational interest, and self-regulated learning than those who quizzed at the end.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that when you quiz yourself during study can affect how interested and engaged you stay, not just what you learn.
ai.life_skill: Try breaking your revision into short self-quizzes spaced throughout a study session instead of saving them all for the end.
ai.fact: Quiz timing within a lesson is linked to students’ engagement and self-regulated learning.
ai.caveat: This was a small, non-randomised classroom study, so the results are not proof that quiz timing caused the differences.

items.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain

ai.headline: Older adults who closely follow a Mediterranean diet may have higher levels of two heart- and brain-protecting proteins.
ai.summary: Researchers studied older adults and found that those who closely followed a Mediterranean diet had higher levels of humanin and SHMOOSE, tiny proteins made by mitochondria. These proteins have been linked to protection against heart disease, Alzheimer's disease, and age-related damage.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a possible biological reason why a Mediterranean diet is linked to healthier ageing of the heart and brain.
ai.life_skill: Try eating more Mediterranean-style foods such as vegetables, fruits, wholegrains, nuts, and olive oil.
ai.fact: Humanin and SHMOOSE are tiny proteins produced by mitochondria and have been linked to protection against heart disease, Alzheimer's disease, and age-related damage.

quiz.question: Which diet was linked to higher levels of humanin and SHMOOSE in older adults?
quiz.answer: Older adults who closely followed the Mediterranean diet had higher levels of these proteins.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study, so it cannot prove the diet caused the higher protein levels.

items.title: Can psychedelics soothe an overactive immune system? New meta-analysis investigates

ai.headline: A review suggests psychedelics may affect inflammation and immune responses.
ai.summary: Researchers carried out a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on serotonergic psychedelics such as psilocybin and LSD. They focused on whether these substances have anti-inflammatory and immune-modulating properties.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows scientists are exploring whether drugs known for changing mood and perception might also influence the immune system.
ai.fact: Serotonergic psychedelics such as psilocybin and LSD are being studied for anti-inflammatory and immune-modulating effects.

quiz.question: What did the researchers review psychedelics for?
quiz.answer: They reviewed their anti-inflammatory and immune-modulating properties.

ai.caveat: A single review does not prove psychedelics can treat immune-related conditions.

items.title: Predicting alcohol consumption from resting-state functional connectivity: Feature relevance and the potential of meta-matching.

ai.headline: Brain scans show only weak links between resting brain activity and drinking habits
ai.summary: Researchers used brain scans and machine learning to see if resting-state brain connectivity could predict alcohol consumption scores in 739 people. Both models predicted scores only weakly but significantly, and the brain patterns were only partly reliable across groups.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that brain imaging may hint at drinking-related patterns but is not yet accurate enough to predict individual behaviour.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your own drinking habits affect your wellbeing rather than relying on brain scans to judge risk.
ai.fact: Resting-state functional connectivity contains weak but reproducible signals linked to alcohol consumption scores.

quiz.question: How well did the brain-scan models predict alcohol consumption scores?
quiz.answer: They predicted scores only weakly but significantly, with a correlation of about 0.15.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the predictive link was weak, so it cannot be used to judge individual risk.

items.title: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial

ai.headline: Durvalumab plus chemotherapy before surgery helped most patients with early-stage lung cancer proceed to surgery.
ai.summary: The study tested durvalumab plus chemotherapy given before surgery in people with resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer. Most patients were able to have surgery, with encouraging rates of complete cancer cell disappearance in removed tissue, and continuing treatment with chemoradiotherapy plus durvalumab raised no new safety concerns for those whose tumours remained unresectable.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how combining immunotherapy with chemotherapy may improve treatment options for people with early-stage lung cancer.
ai.fact: Neoadjuvant treatment means therapy given before the main treatment, such as surgery.

quiz.question: What happened for most patients in the trial after receiving durvalumab plus chemotherapy before surgery?
quiz.answer: Most patients were able to proceed to surgery.

ai.caveat: This is a single phase 2 trial, so the results are encouraging but not yet definitive proof.

items.title: New evidence suggests spinosaurus spent most of its life underwater

ai.headline: New analysis suggests Spinosaurus was mostly aquatic, while some marine reptiles spent time on land.
ai.summary: Yale scientists used machine learning on thousands of fossil measurements to study how prehistoric animals adapted to water. The findings indicate Spinosaurus likely spent most of its life underwater, whereas some ancient marine reptiles previously thought to be fully aquatic actually spent considerable time on land.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that evolutionary paths are not always one-way streets, as animals can return to aquatic lifestyles after living on land for millions of years.
ai.life_skill: Notice that initial assumptions about a category (like 'marine reptile') might be wrong when new data is applied.
ai.fact: Spinosaurus is suggested to have spent most of its life underwater, unlike some other marine reptiles that spent time on land.

quiz.question: What did the study suggest about some ancient marine reptiles?
quiz.answer: Some ancient marine reptiles previously thought to be fully aquatic actually spent considerable time on land.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising a study, so the specific methodological details and peer-review status of the original Yale research are not provided here.

items.title: What are microchimeric cells doing to our brain?

ai.summary: The article explores microchimeric cells—cells exchanged during pregnancy—that can take up residency in the brain. It asks whether these cells could influence development, health, or behaviour. It does not report results from a specific study.

ai.fact: Cells exchanged during pregnancy can take up residency in the human brain.

quiz.answer: They can take up residency in the brain.

items.title: The AI Paradox: How Optimization May Undermine Meaningful Work in Helping Professions

ai.headline: AI may undermine meaningful work
ai.summary: Researchers studied the impact of AI on helping professions, finding that automation may concentrate on tasks that give workers a sense of meaning. items.title: Sarcopenia Is Associated With Severe Treatment Toxicity and Mortality in Older Adults With Advanced Cancer: A Secondary Analysis
items.venue: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle

ai.headline: Older adults with advanced cancer who have sarcopenia face higher severe treatment toxicity and lower one-year survival.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed 161 people aged 70 or older starting new cancer treatment. Those with sarcopenia—low muscle strength plus low muscle quantity—were more likely to have severe non-blood toxicities and had worse one-year survival than those without sarcopenia. Muscle quantity alone was not significantly linked to these outcomes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that checking both muscle strength and quantity may help identify older cancer patients at higher risk from treatment.
ai.life_skill: If you or someone you know is an older adult starting cancer treatment, ask the care team about assessing muscle strength as well as muscle quantity.
ai.fact: Sarcopenia means a loss of muscle strength, quantity and performance, mainly from ageing or disease.
ai.caveat: This was a secondary analysis of one trial’s usual-care arm, mostly non-Hispanic white participants, so results may not apply to everyone.

items.title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios

ai.headline: Genetic scores linked to education are also linked to children's mental health within families.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study. They found that both cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores were associated with externalising behaviour, such as hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, such as anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that genetic factors linked to schooling are connected to mental health in complex ways within families.
ai.life_skill: Notice that behaviour and mood are influenced by many factors, not just school performance.
ai.fact: Education-related polygenic scores are associated with both externalising and internalising behaviour in youth.

items.title: Parental Dementia History is Associated with Peripheral Immune Aging Rather than Generalized Biological and Brain Age Acceleration in Midlife

ai.headline: Having a parent with dementia is linked to immune cell changes in midlife, not faster brain or general biological aging.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 1,204 middle-aged adults and found that parental dementia history was linked to an expansion of CD8 memory T cells and shorter telomeres, but not to accelerated epigenetic or brain aging. Earlier parental dementia onset was linked to a faster pace of biological aging, while poorer parental cognitive performance was linked to faster epigenetic aging and a larger brain age gap.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that family dementia risk may show up in the immune system during midlife, offering a possible early clue before brain changes appear.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether close relatives developed dementia early or had memory problems, and mention this to a healthcare professional if you are concerned about your own risk.
ai.fact: Parental dementia history was associated with CD8 memory T cell expansion in midlife adults.

quiz.question: What did the study find about parental dementia history and brain aging in midlife adults?
quiz.answer: Parental dementia history was not associated with accelerated brain aging.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that parental dementia causes immune aging.

items.title: Sex and Subsistence: Income Effects on Risky Sexual Behavior and Partner Selection -- by Natalie Bau, Corinne Low, Bryce Steinberg

ai.headline: Giving female university students monthly cash reduced risky sex and improved partner choice in Zambia.
ai.summary: Researchers ran a randomised trial giving monthly cash assistance to female students at the University of Zambia and tracked their sexual behaviour. Women receiving cash were less likely to have sex, used condoms more often, and those who were not sexually active at the start were much less likely to begin having sex; among those who did have sex, partner quality improved.

ai.life_skill: Notice how money worries might influence your own choices in relationships and consider seeking support if finances are affecting your wellbeing.
ai.fact: A temporary increase in income was linked to less sex, less condomless sex, and better partner quality among female university students in Zambia.

quiz.answer: The likelihood of having sex fell by 43%.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings come from one setting in Zambia, so they may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning

ai.headline: AI agents can improve over time by jointly learning from past memories and reusable skills.

items.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training

ai.headline: A simple AI recipe can teach a humanoid robot to box in about seven minutes of single-GPU training, using a pretrained controller.
